fix(snowflake): parse (+) outer join markers (#8492)

Snowflake accepts the Oracle-style (+) outer join marker in WHERE
clauses, but the Snowflake tokenizer did not register the token, so
`WHERE t1.c1 = t2.c2(+)` was parsed as a call to a function named c2
and generated as `t2.c2()`, silently dropping the outer join.

Register "(+)" as JOIN_MARKER in the Snowflake tokenizer, which also
flips SUPPORTS_COLUMN_JOIN_MARKS for the dialect. The parser now only
sets join_mark when the marker is actually present instead of storing
join_mark=None on every column (and on function expressions returned
through _parse_column), which kept the existing Snowflake AST argument
assertions intact.
